Thanks Marcus. Quick assessment from Sec:
- Telemetry retention: 30 days default for aggregated metrics is acceptable for hosted; if they require shorter retention for logs that include identifiers we need to scope which categories are considered "raw prompts" vs "metrics".
- Aggregation guarantee: we can provide an aggregated export (counters/histograms) but not redact in-line prompts reliably without customer-side defenses. Recommend we offer an anonymization step plus a sample data share for legal review.
- DataVis Analytics: we do not have a prior relationship. Ask them for a copy of their SOC2 Type II and scope (particularly whether they process runtime prompt data). If they only consume aggregated telemetry we're ok with a standard subcontractor review and a monitoring SLA.
- CMEK/KMS: for Dedicated we can enable customer-managed keys; for Hosted we offer KMS integration with limited key access. If Acme needs strict CMEK on hosted we should escalate to Platform — likely an enterprise feature.

Proposed approach:
1) Offer Acme: aggregated metrics only (30d), plus an optional limited-audit sample (escrowed) under tighter controls.
2) Request DataVis SOC2 + scoping questionnaire; hold approval conditional on no raw prompt access.
3) Legal to propose DPA language that allows an exception for aggregated telemetry only.

I'll draft suggested language for Olga to adapt.

— Irene

Thanks — this is helpful. Draft language I'm proposing for the DPA (short form):

"Telemetry. Customer telemetry sent to Redwood for operational monitoring and improvement shall be limited to aggregated metrics and operational logs that do not include customer prompt or completion content. Redwood will retain such telemetry for a maximum of 30 days unless Customer and Redwood agree to an alternate retention period in writing. Subprocessors shall not receive prompt-level data unless explicitly authorized in writing by Customer.

Subprocessors. Any addition of subprocessors (including DataVis Analytics) shall be contingent upon Redwood's receipt of the subprocessor's SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent assurance covering relevant processing activities. Redwood may impose contractual restrictions limiting the subprocessor's access to telemetry to aggregated or pseudonymized data only."

Action items for us:
- Marcus: propose one short paragraph we can send back to Acme that accepts the 30d aggregated telemetry with the DataVis conditional approval path.
- Irene: we'll need the exact scope text you mentioned to state what we consider "raw prompts" vs "aggregated metrics".
- Laura: update privacy questionnaire sections to reflect the conditional DataVis approval and KMS notes.

If nobody objects I'll send this back to Marie with a proposed DocuSign path and a JIRA SEC ticket to track the subproc evidence (SEC-4321).

Olga

Marie — thanks for sending this over and apologies for the delay. We've reviewed the redline with Security and Legal and can propose the following limited signoff path to keep your timeline:

1) Telemetry: Redwood will accept a 30-day retention window for aggregated operational telemetry. We will not share prompt-level content with 3rd parties. For clarity, "aggregated telemetry" includes counters, latency histograms, error rates, and anonymized model-level usage summaries; it excludes unredacted prompt or completion text.
2) Subprocessor (DataVis Analytics): Approval is conditional. Please have DataVis provide their SOC 2 Type II report and fill the subprocessor questionnaire (link below). Upon receipt and review we will confirm or propose compensating controls.
3) KMS/CMEK: For Dedicated deployments we can enable customer-managed keys. For hosted we can integrate with your KMS but CMEK on hosted is an enterprise-only feature and will require an addendum.

Suggested next steps:
- Marie to collect DataVis SOC2 + questionnaire by Oct 26.
- Acme/Redwood legal to execute the DPA with the confirmed telemetry language. I'll send a redlined paragraph for insertion (attached).
- I'll open SEC-4321 in JIRA and assign to Irene for the subprocessor evidence review.
